subject: biology
title: Cell specialisation and differentiation
key_idea: As an organism develops, cells **differentiate**: they gain the structures they need for one particular job. A specialised cell is adapted to its function, and having specialised cells makes the whole organism more efficient.

blocks.text: A new organism starts as unspecialised cells. This section covers how they change and why it matters.

items.meaning: The process by which an unspecialised cell becomes a specialised cell.
A cell with the structures it needs to carry out one particular function.
A feature of a cell that helps it do its job.

items: As a cell differentiates, it gains different sub-cellular structures for its function.
Most types of animal cell differentiate at an early stage.
Many plant cells keep the ability to differentiate throughout life.
In mature animals, cell division is mainly for repair and replacement.
Different cells can do different jobs.
This makes the organism more efficient.
The word for an unspecialised cell becoming specialised is **differentiation**.
Differentiated cells do different jobs, so the organism works more efficiently.
Animal cells mostly differentiate early. Many plant cells can differentiate throughout life.

blocks.text: For each cell, learn the adaptation and say how it helps the cell do its job.

rows: Digests the outer layer of the egg so the sperm can enter
Gives 46 chromosomes in the fertilised cell
Carries electrical impulses a long way and connects to other cells
Move mucus in the trachea and the egg in the oviduct

items: Sperm cells swim to the egg and carry chromosomes for fertilisation.
Cells that need a lot of energy have many mitochondria.
Always link an adaptation to its job: "has a tail, so it can swim".

blocks.text: Plant cells are specialised for taking in and transporting water and food.

rows: Large surface area to absorb water and mineral ions
Short distance for water to move in
Release energy for active transport of mineral ions
Hollow tube with no end walls
Water and mineral ions flow through easily
Supports the plant and stops the tube collapsing
Sieve plates: pores in the end walls
Dissolved sugars move from cell to cell

diagram.alt: Tap each specialised cell to see its function and main adaptations, then test yourself. The cells are the sperm cell, egg cell, nerve cell, muscle cell, ciliated cell, root hair cell, xylem cell and phloem cell.

parts.name: Sperm cell
parts.detail: Swims to the egg and carries chromosomes for fertilisation. It has a tail, many mitochondria, enzymes in the acrosome and a streamlined head.

parts.name: Egg cell
parts.detail: Is fertilised by a sperm. It has a haploid nucleus and nutrients in its cytoplasm for the early embryo.

parts.name: Nerve cell
parts.detail: Carries electrical impulses. It has a long axon and branched ends that connect to other cells.

parts.name: Muscle cell
parts.detail: Contracts to cause movement. It has protein fibres that shorten and many mitochondria.

parts.name: Ciliated cell
parts.detail: Moves substances along. Its cilia sweep mucus in the trachea and the egg in the oviduct.

parts.name: Root hair cell
parts.detail: Absorbs water and mineral ions. Its hair-like projection gives a large surface area, and it has many mitochondria.

parts.name: Xylem cell
parts.detail: Carries water and mineral ions up the plant. It is a hollow tube with no end walls and strong walls.

parts.name: Phloem cell
parts.detail: Carries dissolved sugars around the plant. Pores in its end walls let the sugars pass through.

items: Root hair cells have a large surface area to absorb water and mineral ions.
Xylem cells are hollow tubes. Phloem cells have pores in their end walls.
Root hair cells have no chloroplasts because roots are underground and there is no light.

checks.q: Name the process by which an unspecialised cell becomes a specialised cell.
Describe two ways a sperm cell is adapted to its function.
checks.a: Any two from: it has a tail to swim; many mitochondria to release energy; enzymes to digest the egg's outer layer; a streamlined shape; a haploid nucleus with 23 chromosomes.

checks.q: Explain how a root hair cell is adapted to absorb water and mineral ions.
checks.a: It has a long hair-like projection, giving a large surface area, so it can absorb a lot of water and mineral ions. It has many mitochondria to release energy for active transport.

worked_example.question: Explain one way a sperm cell is adapted for its function.
answer_points: It has a tail, so it can swim.
OR it has many mitochondria, to release energy for the sperm to swim.
OR it has enzymes, to penetrate into the egg.
OR it is streamlined, to swim faster.
OR it has 23 chromosomes, to produce 46 chromosomes in the fertilised cell.
worked_example.tip: One mark for a correct adaptation and one for the linked explanation. Do not write that energy is made or produced.

worked_example.question: Sperm B has a larger middle section than sperm A. Explain why sperm B will be more likely to fertilise an egg than sperm A if they were both released at the same time.
answer_points: So sperm B has more mitochondria.
Sperm B can release more energy (it has a faster rate of respiration).
Sperm B swims faster or a greater distance.
worked_example.tip: Any three score one mark each. Build the chain: middle section, mitochondria, energy, swimming.

worked_example.question: Cell differentiation occurs during growth in multicellular organisms. Explain why cell differentiation is important.
answer_points: Differentiated cells can do different jobs or functions.
This allows the organism to become more efficient (or more complex).
worked_example.tip: If no other mark is scored, credit is given for saying that it makes specialised cells.
